defects.description: The loop only sends full batches, so the final partial batch is silently dropped whenever the record count is not a multiple of BatchSize.
defects.why_missed: The suite writes exactly 100, 200, and 0 records, all multiples of the batch size, so the remainder is always zero and the loss never occurs.
defects.severity_rationale: Records are silently lost during ordinary writes with the default configuration.
defects.failure_condition: WriteAll(countingSink, 250 records) -> 250 records: Written=200 sink received=200 err=<nil>

detection_criteria.mechanism: The loop only sends full batches, so the final partial batch is silently dropped whenever the record count is not a multiple of BatchSize.
detection_criteria.proof: Show the record lost, duplicated or corrupted, and the operation sequence that does it.

defects.description: On a sink error the result reports the total record count as Written instead of the records accepted before the failure, so a resume skips the lost batch.

trigger.input: WriteAll(sink that fails on its second call, 300 records)
trigger.actual: 300 records, sink fails on batch 2: Written=300 sink received=100 err=sink unavailable

defects.why_missed: No suite sink ever fails, so the error return is never executed and its Written value is never compared with what the sink accepted.
defects.severity_rationale: A sink failure can make resume skip records that the sink never accepted.
defects.failure_condition: WriteAll(sink that fails on its second call, 300 records) -> 300 records, sink fails on batch 2: Written=300 sink received=100 err=sink unavailable

detection_criteria.mechanism: On a sink error the result reports the total record count as Written instead of the records accepted before the failure, so a resume skips the lost batch.
detection_criteria.proof: Show the injected fault, the expected degradation, and the observed wrong behaviour.
